derived_values.name: DnSignal
derived_values.used_by: entry rule (short) and exit rule (long close)

other_exits: Long position closed when DnSignal is non-zero (if BuyPosClose enabled)
Long position closed when DnTrend is non-zero and DnSignal is zero (if BuyPosClose enabled)
Short position closed when UpSignal is non-zero (if SellPosClose enabled)
Short position closed when UpTrend is non-zero and UpSignal is zero (if SellPosClose enabled)

position_sizing.conditional_logic: MM<0 uses fixed lot size equal to abs(MM); MM>0 uses deposit fraction

custom_logic_notes: BrakeExp custom indicator has 4 buffers: buffer0=UpTrend, buffer1=DnTrend, buffer2=UpSignal, buffer3=DnSignal. Signal logic is truthy-based (non-zero values indicate signal/trend presence). Entry signals trigger both open and close of opposing positions. When no fresh signal but trend buffer is active, only opposing position close is triggered (no new entry). The Recount mechanism retries on data unavailability. TradeAlgorithms.mqh provides BuyPositionOpen, SellPositionOpen, BuyPositionClose, SellPositionClose, GlobalVariableDel_, LoadHistory, and CIsNewBar class.
python_conversion_notes: Must reverse-engineer or obtain the BrakeExp indicator source to reimplement in Python. The indicator takes two double params A=3, B=1 and produces 4 buffers (UpTrend, DnTrend, UpSignal, DnSignal). Entry is on signal buffers being truthy; exit is on opposing signal or opposing trend. TradeAlgorithms.mqh functions need mapping: BuyPositionOpen/SellPositionOpen handle position sizing (MM negative=fixed lot, positive=deposit fraction), SL/TP in points, and signal time gating. Position close functions handle deviation. The new-bar guard and Recount retry pattern are standard and easy to replicate.
